evidence: DEFINING BEHAVIOUR GRADED: the brief's core (instruction.md:1-7: shared pipeline board with one-stage moves, shared order, interview places, conflict refusal naming who, all-or-none bulk + undo, live board within 15 s, conversations with paging/unread/seen/drafts, candidate privacy) is graded directly by functional criteria hro_move_one_stage (w1.5), hro_reorder (1.5), hro_interview_full (1.5), hro_stale_refused (2.5), hro_bulk_move/all_or_none/places, hro_undo_restores/conflict/once, hro_live_board (2.5), hro_msg_exchange, hro_thread_latest/earlier, hro_unread_counts, hro_seen, hro_candidate_private (2.5) (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml lines 50-399). SERVER-BACKED, NOT SAME-ORIGIN: the constraints gate hro_gate_shared (tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:22-24) requires a job+candidate created via UI to be found by the Observer 'in a new independent empty browser context' and states 'A static seed response, a no-op success message, a browser-only save or a job-only app does not satisfy the gate'; functional/polish prompts repeat it and define independence as page.context().browser().newContext(), 'A reload or a second tab of the same context is not independent' (functional/prompt.md:11, polish/prompt.md:11). Shared state is re-read by other people in independent contexts in hro_job_open, hro_add_candidate, hro_reorder ('the new order is what an independent context of another recruiter sees'), hro_stale_refused, hro_live_board, hro_msg_exchange, hro_notes (Aud reads notes), so a localStorage-only app fails the gate and those rows. Nothing demands same-origin; the public network posture is respected. SURVIVES RESTART: hro_restart (functional/judge.toml:401-408) plus protocol D (functional/prompt.md:51) require restart_app then fresh sign-in with jobs, card order per stage, notes, messages and activity unchanged and 'the starting data is not loaded again'; restart_app is wired in functional/judge.toml:14-18 via $APP_RESTART_HELPER exported at tests/test.sh:193, matching the template's tests/test.sh and tools/restart_mcp.py (single-use marker, real kill+relaunch on the same DB_PATH). This matches the public rule 'Order survives a reload, a fresh sign-in and a restart' (hireops_rules.md:59) and instruction.md:15 'keep new work across restarts'. SURVIVES RELOAD / RE-AUTH (client state the brief requires durable): reply drafts across view switch and reload in hro_drafts (functional/judge.toml:366-372); drafts across an ended session and re-sign-in, per-person isolation on the same browser (Mei sees none of Rafael's reply/note drafts; Rafael's are back after re-sign-in) in polish hro_pol_session_resume (polish/judge.toml:53-60, w2.5), matching instruction.md:7 and hireops_rules.md:168-175; unsaved note draft across reload in hro_pol_failed_send (polish/judge.toml:50), matching hireops_rules.md:105-106. Reorder after fresh sign-in is shown by the independent-context readback. Every public durability promise I found has a grader; no criterion demands durability the brief does not ask for. BROKEN APP THAT COULD PASS? (a) localStorage-only board: fails the gate (independent Observer context). (b) In-memory server with no DB: passes gate and most rows but hro_restart = 0 (weight 1.5) - durability is genuinely measured, the deduction is proportionate because the rest of the functional behaviour does work. (c) DB that reseeds on each boot: hro_restart explicitly fails 'starting data is loaded again'. (d) Drafts keyed by conversation only (leak across users) or wiped on sign-out: pass hro_drafts but fail hro_pol_session_resume. CONFORMING ALTERNATIVE THAT COULD FAIL? Server-side drafts, per-tab sessions (polish allows 'use this page's own sign-out instead'), SSE/polling/sockets, any route layout - all accepted; hro_restart compares data, not ids or routes. No rule found that would fail a conforming app on durability. GOLDEN: db.js:3,9,19-20 uses better-sqlite3 at DB_PATH and never reseeds a DB that already holds users; app.js:38-43 keys drafts by user id in localStorage. Hashes of db.js (0367a73b...), app.js (6ce330f3...), threads.js (a013ecaa...), index.js (b07109f8...), server.js (4fc5d2c4...) in the frozen task equal raw-evidence-index matching_source_files; workspace.cjs (749036d0...) and results/workspace.json (1c7e6fcc...) hashes re-verified. results/workspace.json records passed=true for 'restart keeps jobs, cards, order, messages and activity without reseeding; live updates resume', 'session ended mid-draft: sign-in prompt, nothing sent, same person resumes and sends; another person sees no draft' and 'drafts kept per conversation across switch and reload' - scripted golden observations only (index scope: 'Not a configured judge run, Oracle grade, model score or judge-duration measurement'). RISK (why risk=true despite Pass on design): the durability proof hro_restart lives in protocol D, which the functional prompt runs LAST after protocols Z,S,M,L,C,B,N,T,U,K,R,V,A in one 9000 s batched judge (functional/judge.toml:4). No full configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent'), so it is unmeasured whether the configured judge reaches D and calls restart_app within budget; if it does not, hro_restart returns 'NOT EXERCISED' = 0 for every submission, including the golden, and restart-durability is then not discriminating. This is required missing runtime evidence, not a demonstrated defect. Minor unbounded note (not a defect): unread/read markers and seen marks are not re-checked after restart in hro_restart; the brief does not single them out as restart-durable beyond 'keep new work', and messages/notes/order/activity are covered.
